item.title: ‘Daddy loves you specially,’ — D’banj remembers late son eight years after death
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian music star Oladapo Daniel Oyebanjo, popularly known as D’banj, has paid an emotional tribute to his late son, Daniel Oyebanjo III, eight years after his tragic death. The singer took to his Instagram page to remember the toddler, fondly known as Daniel D3rd, expressing his enduring love for him and reflecting on how the family has continued to cope with the loss. In his tribute, D’banj said he missed his son but expressed gratitude that he, his wife and their other children were now in a safe place. “I miss you Daniel D3rd my son and trust me I can’t imagine how your mother feels but we are in a Safe Space now THANK YOU …” he wrote. The entertainer also described Daniel as the family’s star boy, adding that the experience had taught him important lessons about life. “Omo Baba Eh, our family’s star boy. “But thank you I’m in a Safe space and so is your mother and your brother and sister, I’m sure you are Proud of us. “Thank you for Showing me what life Really is as a WHOLE.” D’banj further remembered his late uncle, Femi, in the tribute, asking his son to pass a message to him. “Say hi to your Uncle Femi, telll him I miss him too.” Expressing his affection for the deceased toddler, the singer added: “Daddy loves you Specially, Physically, Spiritually and Powerfully.” He signed off the message as “Your Dad Daniel D2nd Lee, The No 1 Entertainer Ever liveth.” Daniel died on June 24, 2018, at the age of 13 months after reportedly drowning in a swimming pool at the family’s residence in Ikoyi, Lagos. His death deeply affected D’banj and his wife, Lineo Didi Kilgrow, who have since continued to rebuild their lives following the devastating incident. The singer’s latest tribute has drawn emotional reactions from fans and well-wishers, many of whom have expressed sympathy and support for the family. item.title: Sowore, police clash over account of attack in Ekiti
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela & Ayobami Okerinde The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has disputed the Ekiti State Police Command’s account of an incident in which he sustained injuries at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, insisting that he and his associates were attacked by suspected political thugs. The police had dismissed reports that Sowore was kidnapped by armed men in the state capital, describing the incident as an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant around the Dalimore area of the state. However, Sowore, in a post on X on Friday, accused the police of downplaying the incident, rejecting the description of the attack as an altercation. He accompanied the post with a video allegedly showing Ekiti State Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, leaving what appeared to be a hospital emergency room after visiting him. Sowore wrote, “The Commissioner of @PoliceNG in Ekiti State, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, personally visited the scene of the brutal attack against us in Ado-Ekiti today. He saw firsthand the extensive injuries we sustained, yet he has the audacity to issue a despicable statement describing a coordinated, violent attack as a mere ‘altercation.’ “THERE WAS NO ALTERCATION! WE WERE ATTACKED! “The Commissioner saw the injuries, witnessed the aftermath of the violence, and was fully aware of the seriousness of what happened. Yet his Command has chosen to trivialize the attack, even describing the injuries as ‘minor.” Earlier, Sowore had raised the alarm in another post on X, claiming that he had been kidnapped by armed thugs and that his whereabouts were unknown. The Ekiti State Police Command, however, dismissed the claim in a statement issued by its Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, saying preliminary information indicated that Sowore had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant. According to the police, officers were alerted and swiftly mobilised to the scene, where they rescued Sowore and took him to the Police Hospital in Ado-Ekiti for medical attention. The statement read, “The attention of the Ekiti State Police Command has been drawn to a message circulating on social media alleging that Mr. Omoyele Sowore, the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate in the forthcoming presidential election, was kidnapped by armed thugs in Ado-Ekiti, with his whereabouts unknown. “The Command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant around Dalimore area, Ado-Ekiti, following which the Police were immediately alerted. “Upon receiving the report, Police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. item.title: Trump reinstates rallies in Kansas, Iowa before midterms
item.description: US President Donald Trump has put campaign rallies in Kansas and Iowa back on the schedule for Sunday — two days before the midterm elections — after abruptly canceling both appearances, a Republican source told AFP Friday. “The rallies are back on. President Trump loves his supporters, and in addition to nearly 20 tele-rallies, he will hold back-to-back rallies in Kansas and Iowa on Sunday,” a party source familiar with Trump’s weekend planning said. Trump had originally been scheduled to campaign in Salina, Kansas, on Saturday and Dubuque, Iowa, on Sunday, but both appearances were scrapped on Thursday, with Republicans saying he would instead concentrate on telephone rallies. The sudden changes raised questions about the 80-year-old president’s health and stamina, prompting an angry response when a reporter asked whether he was feeling well. “I feel perfect,” Trump snapped, saying he no longer needed to visit Kansas because Republican Senator Roger Marshall was “doing very well.” Marshall faces an unexpectedly competitive challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton in Kansas, which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932. In Iowa, Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson is fighting a close race against Democrat Josh Turek. Both states voted comfortably for Trump in 2024, but have emerged as battlegrounds in the fight for control of the Senate. Republicans are defending their 53-47 majority in the Senate in Tuesday’s elections, while Democrats are seeking to capture at least one chamber of Congress and curb Trump’s legislative agenda during his final two years in office. Political strategist Mike Fahey, a veteran of multiple election campaigns, told AFP Trump’s about-face was likely the result of the questions over his energy levels. “My suspicion is that Trump didn’t particularly like that narrative, and putting the events back on the calendar was the fastest way to kill it,” he said. “There’s also a legitimate campaign strategy argument here… A phone call doesn’t generate the same local headlines, television coverage or excitement as Air Force One landing in your state three days before an election.” The post Trump reinstates rallies in Kansas, Iowa before midterms appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How Young Nigerians Are Building Businesses Before They Raise Money
item.description: “Zero-capital business” is a loose description. Mobile data, transport, electricity, and time all cost money, and no national dataset shows how many Nigerian firms literally started from nothing. The clearer trend is different: more young people are trying to make a first sale before taking a loan, renting a shop, or filling a storeroom. Moniepoint’s 2025 informal-economy report found that 38% of operators went into business because they could not find work, while its earlier research put 57.7% of informal-business owners below age 34. Credit Is Still an Expensive First Step The Central Bank of Nigeria cut its Monetary Policy Rate to 23% in September 2026 after leaving it at 26.5% in July. That rate is not the same as the borrowing cost a small trader sees at street level, but it still shapes credit conditions across the system. At the same time, 79% of informal businesses surveyed by Moniepoint said their operating costs had risen over the previous year. For a first-time founder, taking on debt before finding customers can be a rough way to begin. Sell Something Before Buying Something Service work has changed the order in which money gets spent. A video editor, developer, designer, or social-media manager can land a project before paying for inventory, and Nigeria’s 3MTT program has been training people in software development, product design, data analysis, cybersecurity, and digital marketing. In October 2025, the 3MTT–NJFP Placement Initiative began linking trained talent with employers at no recruitment or onboarding cost to participating firms. Skills can now be tested in the market before the business has much of a balance sheet. One Phone Can Handle the First Customer For many young founders, the first storefront is a chat thread. Orders come in on WhatsApp, product photos sit on Instagram, and a bank transfer can close the deal before anyone pays for shelves, rent, or a cashier’s desk. Moniepoint found that cash still dominates many customer purchases, but 48% of informal-business owners said they preferred transfers when paying other businesses. The same habit of doing more on one device shows up in consumer platforms too: an adult using Melbet can move between sports markets and casino products on a phone instead of going to a betting shop, though any personal play still belongs in a separate entertainment bankroll, not in business cash. Pre-Orders Let Demand Speak First A lot of young sellers now ask the market a question before they spend real money on stock. A fashion seller can collect deposits before buying fabric, and a food vendor can cook against booked deliveries instead of guessing how many walk-in customers might appear. That caution fits the numbers: Moniepoint’s 2025 survey found that 44% of informal businesses reported daily revenue below ₦20,000. item.title: South African court sets limits on anti-migrant demonstration
item.description: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside a court in South Africa’s coastal city of Durban on Friday as the government sought judicial intervention to rein in anti-migrant demonstrations that have turned deadly, leaving one person dead last week. Durban, the Zulu heartland, has emerged as a focal point of anti-migrant agitation led by the March and March movement, which has organised demonstrations against undocumented foreigners across the country for months. Some demonstrations have turned violent, including last week when a mob of about 50 people beat a foreign national to death, prompting President Cyril Ramaphosa to deploy more than 500 soldiers to support the police. Protesters sang and chanted outside the high court, waving placards reading “reclaim our country” and sticks as police officers kept a close watch. Supporters of several political parties, including the centre-right ActionSA and the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party led by former president Jacob Zuma, also turned out in solidarity. Judge Peter Olsen allowed March and March movement to proceed with its planned demonstrations, but under tighter conditions following amendments to the government’s application. Under the revised terms, the group may march between 9am and 3pm, with participants barred from carrying weapons or covering their faces. The group was also prohibited from destroying property or setting fire to buildings. The matter is expected to return to court next year. The court action was brought by acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia, who was seeking to stop the demonstrations on the grounds that they threaten public order and the safety of foreign nationals. He cited police intelligence about an alleged plot to set fire to the Home Affairs Refugee Reception Centre in Berea, an inner-city suburb of Durban where asylum seekers go to seek documentation. The unrest has been fuelled by misinformation about a July Constitutional Court ruling that asylum seekers cannot be denied access to South Africa’s asylum system solely on procedural grounds, according to the police. – ‘Widespread violence’ – Counsel for the police told the court on Friday that the situation in Durban had “degenerated into lawlessness” that reactive policing could no longer contain. More than 400 police officers had been deployed, but this had “proved structurally unable to stem the widespread violence”, they said. March and March defended its right to demonstrate under the constitution, distancing itself from the violence and insisting it should not be held responsible for the actions of those involved. “The agenda is to try and silence the people,” March and March legal representative Xolani Zuma told reporters ahead of the court decision. “The real problem are illegal immigrants who are here in the country and terrorising people,” he said. item.title: Nigeria, Russia Review 1967 Bilateral Air Services Agreement
item.description: Nigeria on Friday met with the Russian Federation on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Russia, as both countries move to strengthen aviation relations and expand cooperation in the air transport sector. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, led Nigeria’s delegation to a high-level bilateral meeting. At the meeting, the Nigerian delegation, led by Keyamo, held discussions with Dmitry Stanislavovich Zverev, who is the State Secretary and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Russian Federation, on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. A major outcome of the meeting was the resolution by both sides to renegotiate the Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA) between Nigeria and Russia, which dates back to 1967, with a view to establishing a new agreement that reflects contemporary developments and emerging opportunities in international aviation. The meeting centred on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. According to a statement by the aviation ministry, both countries agreed on a six-month timeline to conclude the negotiations and sign the new agreement in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in April 2027. To facilitate the process, the two sides have constituted their respective negotiating teams to commence work immediately and ensure that the agreed timeline is met. “The proposed agreement is expected to provide an updated framework for bilateral air transport relations and create opportunities for enhanced connectivity, closer institutional collaboration and mutually beneficial engagement between the aviation sectors of both countries,” the statement signed by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood. The Nigerian delegation included the Director-General of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Capt. Chris Najomo; the Registrar of the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT), Dr. Danjuma Adamu Ismaila, as well as directors from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA. “Beyond the review of the existing air services agreement, the meeting also explored other potential areas of cooperation between Nigeria and Russia,” the statement disclosed. It added that both parties expressed their commitment to examining the opportunities in the coming months, with a view to deepening bilateral relations and identifying areas of shared interest in aviation and related sectors. item.title: Pope Leo makes history with US midterm vote
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, the Catholic Church’s first US-born pontiff, has voted in the United States midterm elections, the first known time a pope has voted in a political election. The head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who has clashed with US President Donald Trump, submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago, the Vatican said Friday. The Chicago-born pontiff “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so” and believes in “the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it said. A rift earlier this year between US President Donald Trump and the pope sparked global headlines. Leo and Trump repeatedly clashed over papal criticism of the harsh crackdown on immigration in the United States and of the war on Iran, with Trump calling the pontiff “weak” on crime and “terrible” on foreign policy. The pope said he was “not afraid” of Trump. In April, after Trump’s threat to destroy Iran, Leo called on everyone to do their part for peace, urging them to “contact the authorities — political leaders, congressmen — to ask them, to tell them, to work for peace and to reject war and violence.” The crucial US midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3. In September, Leo urged the faithful to shake off “all passivity and indifference” toward current events. “We cannot remain as unengaged spectators; rather, we must listen with our hearts, allow ourselves to be challenged, and become involved,” he said during the weekly general audience in St Peter’s Square. Robert Francis Prevost, as he was known before his papal election, voted in Democratic primaries in 2008 and 2010 and in three Republican primaries in the years that followed, according to the New York Times, citing state and local records. In primary elections in Illinois, voters may choose any party’s ballot at the polls, and Prevost varied in his selection, it said. Prevost spent nearly two decades as a missionary in Peru and has both US and Peruvian citizenship. “The Holy Father has also confirmed that, during his years of residence in Peru he exercised his right to vote whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Vatican said. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s son unveils plan for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: Alhaji Abba Abubakar, son of former Vice-President Atiku, on Friday unveiled his 2027 mobilisation plan in the six geo-political zones for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. The former vice-president’s son who is the founder and chairman of Haske Bola Tinubu Organisation (HBTO) a political mobilisation and support platform in Abuja at the All Progressives Congress (APC) National Secretariat had earlier defected to the party. “Looking ahead, HBTO is preparing for an ambitious nationwide political mobilisation programme. “As part of this strategy, we intend to commence a two-million-man mobilisation march across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones, beginning from Abuja. “Our immediate mobilisation efforts will focus on supporting the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, whom we recognise as a key political leader in our mobilisation structure in the collective effort to secure Tinubu’s victory in the FCT in 2027. “We are also working in alignment with the FCT minister’s political objective of delivering both the FCT and Rivers for President Tinubu in the forthcoming election,” Abubakar said. The former vice-president’s son added that his organisation was preparing for a major political mobilisation in Rivers in the first week of November. He added that as part of its commitment to complement the Tinubu reform agenda with practical interventions, his organisation was introducing a transportation support initiative through the initial provision of ten luxury buses. He said the initiative was designed to ease transportation challenges, reduce the burden of commuting on ordinary Nigerians and demonstrate that political support must go beyond rhetoric to include tangible contributions to the lives of citizens. “We intend to commence this programme in the FCT before progressively expanding the initiative to other parts of the federation. “For us, supporting the president’s Renewed Hope Agenda must translate into meaningful actions that positively affect the everyday lives of Nigerians,” he said. According to him, his organisation’s structures are already being activated, and its members are on the ground while its supporters are ready to demonstrate its strength and reach. “This is not simply about numbers or political appearances, it is about building a disciplined, coordinated and effective grassroots mobilisation network capable of translating political support into electoral results. He said the organisation intends to establish its presence across the geopolitical zones, strengthen its state and zonal structures, engage community stakeholders and work collaboratively with other progressive political forces to ensure Tinubu’s re-election. He said political conviction was a matter of personal judgement, conscience and the freedom of every individual to make independent choices. item.title: Flick praises Yamal ‘mentality’ after missing out on Ballon d’Or
item.description: Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal has “reacted very well” following the disappointment of the Ballon d’Or being awarded to Harry Kane, his coach Hansi Flick said on Friday. Despite winning La Liga with the Catalan club and lifting the World Cup with Spain, the 19-year-old winger came third in the vote for the best player in the world on Monday, behind Kane and Kylian Mbappe. “Harry Kane deserved it, but you already know what I think about Lamine. He’s at the level required to win this award,” Flick said ahead of the La Liga leaders’ home match against Alaves. “I’m very proud of Lamine. He reacted very well and was very focused in training. “That’s the way to respond. His mentality is very good for the team.” Yamal will have a chance to put any lingering disappointment behind him on Saturday when Barcelona will look to correct course at home to Alaves following two high-profile defeats. After winning their first 11 matches in all competitions, Barcelona were flying but then came undone when they travelled to PSG in the Champions League last Tuesday. That 4-2 reverse in the French capital was swiftly followed up by a Kylian Mbappe-inspired 2-1 loss at home to Real Madrid in La Liga last weekend. “The most important thing tomorrow is to win,” Flick said. “The team is playing well and we believe in our strengths. I’ve seen a good training session and a positive mood. We have to show that tomorrow. “Alaves are a team that know how to defend well, but we’re Barca and we want to show our best version.” Barcelona still hold a two-point lead at the top of La Liga ahead of their meeting with Atletico Madrid. While the German coach admitted he does not like losing, he insisted that the campaign is “a long road”. “It’s at the end of the season that we can win trophies,” he added. “We have to deal with it. We could have won, but we have to accept defeat and learn from it.” The post Flick praises Yamal ‘mentality’ after missing out on Ballon d’Or appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sowunmi challenges Utomi over claim Obi will strengthen naira to N500/$1
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Segun Sowunmi, has faulted Pat Utomi’s claim that Peter Obi could strengthen the naira to ₦500 per dollar if elected president. In a post on X on Friday, Sowunmi described the proposal as “a textbook example of confusing political aspiration with economic feasibility” and questioned how the exchange-rate target and promised price cuts would be achieved. Utomi, a political economist and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), had said the target would feature in Obi’s manifesto. “We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he wrote on X on Thursday. He said the proposal would help curb inflation, reduce poverty and lower the cost of living. With investments in security, electricity and roads, alongside market reforms, Utomi projected that prices of staples including bread, rice, yam, maize, plantain, chicken, eggs and garri could fall by about half. Reacting, Sowunmi asked how the government would secure enough foreign exchange to sustain the proposed rate. “Where is the additional foreign exchange coming from? What will finance the proposed intervention?” he asked. He said exchange rates are shaped by “foreign-exchange supply and demand, productivity, export earnings, capital flows, monetary conditions and confidence in the economy”. He added that the listed commodities had “fundamentally different cost structures” and that a stronger naira “cannot automatically halve the cost of domestically produced commodities”. Sowunmi also disputed Utomi’s cement projection, saying a $10 bag would cost ₦5,000 at ₦500 to the dollar, not ₦2,000. “To arrive at ₦2,000, the authors have additionally assumed a 60% reduction in the dollar-denominated price. Where is the economic justification for that assumption?” he said. He warned that currency appreciation without productivity gains could make imports more attractive and weaken local manufacturers. A serious manifesto, he said, must explain how its policies would work, including their assumptions, costs, timelines and measurable targets. Sowunmi said reducing living costs and poverty was a legitimate ambition, but required productivity growth, stronger agriculture and industry, reliable electricity, infrastructure, security, job creation and sound economic management. “The naira should become stronger because the Nigerian economy has become stronger, not because somebody has decided that ₦500 to the dollar would make an attractive manifesto headline,” he added. item.title: NDC defends Obi’s single-term pledge, dismisses Okorocha’s ‘gambling’ claim
item.description: By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has thrown its weight behind the single-term presidential pledge by its Presidential candidate ahead of January 16 2027. Peter Obi. The NDC described describing it as a constitutional commitment to performance, national stability and leadership accountability rather than a political gamble, adding that Obi had voluntarily offered to serve only one term, subjecting his leadership to public assessment based on results rather than political calculations. The party noted that Nigeria’s experience with an eight-year presidential administration between 2015 and 2023 demonstrated that longevity in office did not automatically translate into improved governance or national development, adding that the period was characterised by rising inflation, naira depreciation, increasing public debt, widespread poverty and insecurity In a statement signed on Friday by NDC Director-General of the National Presidential Campaign Council, NPCC, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim, the party disagreed with Okorocha’s characterisation of the pledge as “a four-year gambling”, insisting that the proposal was constitutionally permissible and represented a deliberate commitment to deliver measurable results within four years. According to him, Section 135(2) of the 1999 Constitution provides for a four-year presidential tenure with the possibility of seeking another term, arguing that the provision does not make a second term compulsory. The leadership of the NDC was reacting to comments by former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he described Obi as “a fantastic gentleman; clear in his head” but questioned the viability of his proposed single-term presidency. The party maintained that Obi’s single-term proposal was designed to shift the focus of presidential leadership from the duration of stay in office to measurable achievements and effective delivery of campaign promises. Describing the pledge as a performance commitment, He said, “Section 135(2) of the 1999 Constitution provides that a President shall leave office after four years and may seek a further four years. In law, ‘may’ is permissive, not mandatory. A single term is therefore constitutional. It is not a gamble. “Nigeria already tested an eight-year tenure between 2015 and 2023. The result was rising inflation, a weakened naira, soaring public debt, widespread poverty, and insecurity across the country. That is the real balance sheet of prolonged tenure without performance. “Peter Obi’s offer is a performance bond, not a gamble. He has pledged to serve one term, to be judged strictly by results, and to hand over power in 2031 in recognition that it is the turn of the North. item.title: 2027: INEC receives over 4,800 claims, 600 objections on voter register
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has received over 4,800 claims and about 600 objections on the preliminary voter register, with a promise that the discrepancies will be corrected before the final register is certified on December 15, 2026. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this on Friday when the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission paid a courtesy visit to the commission’s headquarters in Abuja. The mission is led by Victor Bockarie Foh, a former Vice-President of Sierra Leone. Amupitan said the claims, received at the registration areas where the register was displayed as of Thursday, were mainly corrections and other minor matters. On objections, he said the commission had received “about 600 complaints on the register” through electoral officers and Resident Electoral Commissioners from the various wards. He added that “the display of the register online is also confirming some of the complaints we had earlier received.” According to hum, the register now stands at over 103 million registered citizens, adding that it is a huge figure, and that the discrepancies noticed would be corrected so that “the register will be properly cleaned up” ahead of the final list. The commission completed three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise and recently ended the physical display of the preliminary register at registration areas nationwide. It has also published the register on its online portal, display.inecnigeria.org, “for public scrutiny, claims, and objections.” He again restated that the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are scheduled for Saturday, February 6, 2027. He said the commission will deploy personnel and technology across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, covering 774 Local Government Areas, 8,809 Registration Areas (Wards) and 176,846 polling units. Amupitan said the commission had executed nine of the 14 major milestones in its Revised Timetable and Schedule of Activities for the election. He said INEC had also moved “away from administrative assumptions” by personally conducting zonal readiness assessment tours. It has covered the South-West in Lagos, the North-West in Kaduna, the South-East in Enugu and the North-East in Gombe, and the team is heading to Port Harcourt for the South-South. The North-Central, the last zone, will be visited next week. He said the tours had shown that some areas needed higher deployments than planned because of terrain and security challenges. item.title: Ancelotti omits Alisson as Brazil name squad for November friendlies
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti has named a youthful 26-man squad for November friendlies against Japan and Singapore, leaving out Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker while insisting he remains the country’s best goalkeeper. The squad was announced on Thursday at the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) headquarters in Rio de Janeiro. Brazil will face Japan on November 14 and Singapore three days later, as Ancelotti continues rebuilding the team after its disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign. “We don’t need to test Alisson. We know him very well. He’s the best goalkeeper,” Ancelotti said. “When the Copa América starts, he’ll be called up. Like Alisson, all the others will be.” Ancelotti said the November matches would give him an opportunity to assess younger players and refresh the squad. The selection includes nine players of Olympic age and 15 under 23. “We need to make the most of 2027 to carry out this renewal,” he said, adding that he expected Brazil to have a more established team by the time preparations for the 2028 Copa América and World Cup qualifying intensify. Chelsea forward Estêvão has retained his place despite limited playing time at club level. Ancelotti said Brazil would continue monitoring the 19-year-old and allow him to develop at his own pace. The squad also includes maiden call-ups for Corinthians midfielder André and Cruzeiro defender Jonathan Jesus. Manchester City forward Allan is among the other young players selected. No players from Flamengo or Palmeiras were called up following an agreement with the CBF, as the clubs are competing in a tight domestic title race. Atlético Mineiro players were also left out. Full Squad: Goalkeepers: Bento (Al Nassr), Lucas Perri (Torino), Pedro Morisco (Coritiba). Defenders: Arthur Dias (Athletico Paranaense), Carlos Augusto (Inter Milan), Douglas Santos (Zenit), Gabriel Magalhães (Arsenal), Jair Cunha (Nottingham Forest), Jonathan Jesus (Cruzeiro), Vanderson (Monaco), Vitor Reis (Manchester City), Wesley (Roma). Midfielders: André (Corinthians), Andrey Santos (Manchester United), Bruno Guimarães (Arsenal), Danilo (Botafogo), Gabriel Bontempo (Santos), João Gomes (Aston Villa), Marlon Gomes (Shakhtar Donetsk). Forwards: Alisson Santana (Shakhtar Donetsk), Allan (Manchester City), Estêvão (Chelsea), Raphinha (Barcelona), Rayan (Bournemouth), Endrick and Vinícius Júnior (both Real Madrid). item.title: [VIDEO] N70,000 Allowance: Ajaero Cannot Negotiate On Behalf Of Organised Labour — Osifo
item.description: The President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), Festus Osifo, has said his Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC) counterpart, Joe Ajaero, cannot negotiate on behalf of organised labour, insisting that he can only speak for NLC members. Osifo spoke on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Friday, following the disagreement between the two labour leaders over the Federal Government’s proposed ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers for six months. Ajaero had criticised Osifo for rejecting the offer, arguing that the TUC had no right to turn it down. However, Osifo maintained that the TUC had its own position on the offer and that Ajaero could not negotiate on behalf of its members. “Comrade Ajaero does not have the right to negotiate on behalf of organised labour and TUC members. He has the right to negotiate for Nigerian Labour Congress members,” he said. ﻿ Osifo explained that the TUC’s rejection of the allowance was not based on any document signed by Ajaero, saying the congress had communicated its position to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation before the NLC president’s meeting with the Federal Ministry of Labour. “Our rejection was not as a result of the document Ajaero signed. We already took that position with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation earlier on. He never negotiated for it; it was the President of the Federal Republic that gave that,” he said. The TUC president said the congress had proposed a ₦300,000 salary increase but was offered the ₦70,000 transport allowance for six months instead. He said the TUC had rejected the allowance before Ajaero met with the Federal Ministry of Labour and announced the offer. “The ₦70k is something we had rejected earlier before Ajaero had his meeting with the Federal Ministry of Labour,” Osifo said. He maintained that the TUC’s immediate demand was a salary increase, arguing that the Federal Government could raise workers’ pay while discussions on a new minimum wage were pending. “Since it takes time to negotiate minimum wage and there is no law in Nigeria that stipulates maximum wage, some states are currently paying more than the current minimum wage. We can pull the Federal Government to increase the pay of workers,” he said. Osifo said the TUC’s position remained unchanged and had been communicated at a press conference on October 8, 2026. He added that the congress expected minimum wage review discussions to begin in February. item.title: NDC urges INEC to remove deceased Nigerians from voters’ register
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove the names of deceased Nigerians from the voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party’s National Presidential Campaign Council (NPCC) raised concerns over reports that deceased Nigerians, including prominent figures such as Raymond Dokpesi, Ifeanyi Ubah, Muhammadu Buhari and Rotimi Akeredolu, still appear on the register. In a statement on Friday, signed by its spokesperson, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, the council questioned the accuracy and integrity of the voters’ register and called on INEC to explain when it was last comprehensively updated. The council also urged Nigerians and political parties to exercise their legal rights by filing objections against names believed to have been wrongly retained on the register. It called on INEC to establish an online portal for publishing names under objection, allowing affected individuals who are alive to respond, and making public the procedure for challenging questionable entries. The statement read: “Reports that deceased Nigerians, including prominent figures such as Raymond Dokpesi, Ifeanyi Ubah, Muhammadu Buhari and Rotimi Akeredolu, still appear on the voters’ register raise serious questions about its accuracy and integrity. “These are just a few names. What about the 774 local government areas across Nigeria? How many deceased persons remain on the register? When was it last comprehensively updated? Is this an oversight, institutional failure or something more troubling? “INEC has the legal responsibility to cleanse the register, especially if it has been notified by citizens. The electoral body owes Nigerians answers. We demand a credible, up-to-date and verifiable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 elections.” The council said INEC, as a publicly funded institution, must demonstrate efficiency, professionalism and accountability in managing the electoral register. It further called for an independent audit of INEC’s processes and mechanisms, citing concerns over the credibility of the 2023 general elections. “The 2027 election is too critical for unanswered questions about the very foundation of our democracy. No excuses. No complacency. No questionable register. INEC must do its job,” the statement added. item.title: How Dangote Refinery’s ₦2.15trn IPO Ambition Moved Beyond Physical Borders
item.description: The story of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has always been about scale. A vast industrial complex rose on the outskirts of Lagos, promising to reshape Nigeria’s refining capacity. Three years after its inauguration, that ambition entered a new chapter: opening the doors to investors across Africa and beyond. When the refinery’s initial public offering (IPO) closed on October 27, 2026, it had attracted investor applications from 120 countries, including all 54 African nations. The company described the response as a milestone for African capital markets, with applications spanning all six continents. L-R: Group Chairman, Nigerian Exchange Group, Umaru Kwairanga; President and Chief Executive Officer, Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote; Group Executive Director, Dangote Industries Limited, Halima Aliko-Dangote; Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Nigerian Exchange Group, Temi Popoola, at the official opening of the Dangote Refinery IPO at the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) in Lagos on Monday, September 14, 2026. Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels Television. For Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, the significance extended beyond the money raised. It was about who could participate in the value created by an African-built industrial enterprise. “To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It shows our people don’t just want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it, and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” said Dangote. An Industrial Ambition The refinery was officially inaugurated on May 22, 2023, by then-President Muhammadu Buhari at the Lekki Free Zone in Lagos. Built over nearly a decade, the project represented an investment of approximately $20 billion. At the inauguration, the scale of the project prompted expectations that Nigeria could strengthen domestic fuel supply and reduce its reliance on imported refined petroleum products. The facility was initially designed as a 650,000-barrel-per-day refinery and petrochemical complex, making it one of Africa’s largest industrial investments. Former President Muhammadu Buhari inaugurated the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals in Lagos State on Monday, May 22, 2023. (Photo: State House) Production began in January 2024, initially with diesel and aviation fuel before the planned expansion into petrol production. The refinery’s emergence marked a shift from construction and commissioning towards commercial operations. Its significance also extends beyond Nigeria. In March 2026, traders had sold 12 cargoes totalling 456,000 tonnes of refined petroleum products for delivery to markets including Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, Tanzania, Ghana and Togo. Those shipments offered a glimpse of the refinery’s potential role in regional energy trade, connecting Nigeria’s industrial capacity with demand in other African economies.

item.title: 48 terrorists, one soldier killed in foiled attacks on troops in Borno, Yobe
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Barely 24 hours when scores of Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists were killed in separate encounter in communities of Kukawa and Marte local government areas of Borno state, about 48 terrorists were neutralised by Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI while attempting to infiltrate military positions in Bitta Gwoza LGA of Borno State and North East Theatre Training School (NETTS), Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA of Yobe State between 29 and 30 October 2026. Unfortunately, the engagements recorded one soldier who paid the supreme sacrifice, with two others sustained minor injuries. This was disclosed on Friday in a press statement signed by the Acting Media Information Officer Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni. He said: “Troops of OPHK have dealt a major blow to Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists, foiling their attacks on military positions in Bitta Gwoza LGA of Borno State and North East Theatre Training School (NETTS), Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA of Yobe State between 29 and 30 October 2026. “In Bitta, troops decisively disorganised an attempted terrorist assault on the night of 29 October 2026. The combined response of ground troops and air support overwhelmed the attackers, thwarting their plan and inflicting heavy casualties. “In a related development, troops launched a successful counter-attack against a large concentration of ISWAP fighters who attacked NETTS Buni Yadi on same 29 October to the early hours on 30 October 2026. “The approximately five-hour engagement was coordinated by the Theatre Command, with effective integration of Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (ISTAR) capabilities, alongside air and ground assets. “The decisive counter-offensive resulted in 48 terrorists killed, with troops recovering a substantial cache of weapons and ammunition. “Recovered items include 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMG), one 60mm mortar, 105 AK-47 magazines and two video cameras. “Also recovered were 30 rounds of 12.7mm armour-piercing incendiary ammunition, 2,738 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, 223 rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and 2,054 rounds of PKT ammunition. “The engagements recorded one soldier who paid the supreme sacrifice. May his soul rest in peace. Also the two others who sustained minor injuries are responding to treatment. The morale of troops remains high as they sustain operations against terrorist elements across the theatre”. Goni stated. The latest operational successes according to the statement further demonstrate the troops’ combat effectiveness, operational coordination and determination to deny terrorists freedom of action. The heavy losses suffered by the insurgents and the recovery of their weapons and ammunition Goni said, constitute another significant setback to their operational capabilities. item.title: 29-year-old Nigerian man killed as tree crushes car in London
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 29-year-old Nigerian man, James Abiwon, has died after a tree fell on his car during Storm Boelo in Mill Hill, north London. According to Metro UK, Abiwon was driving along Dollis Road at about 12.30pm on Sunday when the tree came down in strong winds. Emergency crews, including police officers, firefighters, paramedics and an air ambulance, responded, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. His cousin, Tyrrell Okolo, described him as “a master of everything” and a devoted family man. Abiwon was a tech sales executive who had earned a degree from the University of Essex. He was also a semi-professional footballer with Aldershot, a musician with about 40,000 YouTube viewers and a mentor to many, his cousin said. Abiwon had been preparing to celebrate his 30th birthday with a padel tournament. The event will now go ahead in his memory, with proceeds going to support his family. His close friend, Kwame Affum, 29, said the two had played padel together just two days before the crash. “I’m trying hard to get my head around this,” he told Metro UK. A friend had messaged Abiwon shortly before the accident about money they owed him for the court, but he did not reply, prompting concern. Affum said Abiwon loved sport, was a good footballer and supported Arsenal. He had earned a first-class university degree and recently won an award at work. “He was full of energy and talent,” Affum said. “He was going to celebrate his 30th birthday in two weeks. It just seems impossible this has happened.” A witness who laid flowers at the scene told Metro UK that she heard a helicopter and went outside to find the fallen tree covering the road, with the car trapped beneath it. Abiwon’s girlfriend and best friend arrived while rescuers were still at the scene. The witness said they were shaking as they waited and hoped he would be brought out. The witness said Abiwon’s aunties and other relatives arrived later and were inconsolable. She described him as clearly well loved and said the community had lost one of its own. Traffic on Dollis Road was reportedly heavy at the time, as roadworks on a nearby street had diverted more vehicles onto the route. A neighbour whose home overlooks the scene said: “If it had been 10 minutes later, it could have been me.” The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to Dollis Road at about 12.40pm on Sunday after reports that a tree had fallen onto a moving car. Police are working with the local authority and coroner to establish the circumstances surrounding Abiwon’s death. Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 84mph across parts of the UK over the weekend. A 60-year-old man was also killed by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, while others were injured. item.title: Flamingos’ World Cup Form Offers Hope For Super Falcons’ Future
item.description: Nigeria’s impressive run at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco offers hope for the Super Falcons’ future as the senior team faces the challenge of transitioning from an established generation to a new crop of players. The Flamingos have reached the quarter-finals after recovering from an opening 2-1 defeat to Poland, beating Puerto Rico 2-0 and defending champions North Korea 3-1 before overcoming Mexico 2-1 in the Round of 16 on Thursday. Oluebube Umejiaku and Mary Dunstan scored to secure the win over Mexico, sending Nigeria into a quarter-final clash against Venezuela on Sunday, November 1. Mary Dunstan celebrates her goal for Flamingos against Mexico. X/@FIFAWWC Beyond their pursuit of a World Cup title, the Flamingos’ performances have offered a glimpse of what Nigeria’s next generation could bring to the senior women’s team. A Generation Showing Promise The need to prepare new players has become increasingly important for the Super Falcons following the departure of experienced internationals. Nigeria’s failure to defend its Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in 2026 has also renewed attention on the team’s future. Youth teams are designed partly to prepare players for senior international football, but the transition is rarely straightforward. Excelling at U-17 level does not guarantee success against older, more experienced opponents. For Nigeria, therefore, the Flamingos’ progress represents an encouraging starting point rather than a guarantee of future success. Flamingos. Photo credit: FIFA Their response to adversity has been particularly noteworthy. After losing to Poland, they bounced back against Puerto Rico before producing one of their biggest statements of the tournament by defeating North Korea, a two-time champion. According to FIFA records, North Korea had gone 2,900 days without a defeat in regulation time at the U-17 Women’s World Cup. Its last such loss came against Germany on November 14, 2018, when it was beaten 4-1. Nigeria ended that run with a commanding 3-1 victory. Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Rodiat Yusuf scored for the Flamingos, while North Korea managed a late consolation from the penalty spot. The result demonstrated Nigeria’s ability to compete against established youth teams. Their subsequent victory over Mexico has reinforced that impression, although the quarter-final against Venezuela will provide another test. Players To Watch Captain Harmony Chidi leads a squad that has produced several encouraging performances. In attack, Adegbuyi and Umejiaku have scored important goals, with Umejiaku also finding the net against Mexico. Yusuf has contributed creatively and scored a free-kick against North Korea, while Dunstan has also made her mark with goals in the tournament. Tosin Rafiu has contributed to the team’s attacking play, while defenders Azeezat Oduntan, Ohunene Sunday and Esther Stephen have featured in Nigeria’s efforts to contain opponents. item.title: ‘I was warned not to buy car or house’ — Nigerian Pastor recounts ritual wealth
item.description: Pastor Joel Olasunkanmi, an Ogbomoso based cleric, has recounted how his pursuit of wealth through ritual practices allegedly led to a life changing car accident that resulted in the amputation of his leg. Olasunkanmi shared his experience during an interview with BBC Yoruba, saying he turned to a ritualist while pursuing what he described as vain and worldly things. According to the pastor, his involvement in the practice lasted about five years, during which he was instructed to find a young woman he deeply loved and carry out a ritual involving her. “Thirty years ago, I took some steps that made God angry. It was while I was searching for vain and worldly things that I became disabled. I had a car accident on May 26, 2001,” he said. Recounting the instructions given to him by the ritualist, Olasunkanmi alleged that he was asked to find a woman he loved, have sexual intercourse with her and use a white handkerchief to wipe her private parts before presenting it to the ritualist. “The ritualist I sought told me to look for a young lady that I so much loved. I searched for her, had sex with her and used a white handkerchief to wipe her genitals. I took it to the man,” he recounted. He said the ritual eventually brought him wealth, although he claimed he did not fully understand how it happened. However, he alleged that the ritualist placed restrictions on how he could spend the money. “I did become rich. I did not know how it happened. But I did become rich. But I was told I could not buy a car or house from it,” he said. The pastor further disclosed that the vehicle involved in the accident that eventually led to the amputation of his leg was indirectly connected to him because he had provided the money used to purchase it for another person. “At the end of the day, the car that hit me was indirectly mine because I was the one who bought it for him. At the end of the day, my leg was amputated,” he said. Reflecting on his experience, Olasunkanmi urged young Nigerians to exercise patience and avoid seeking quick wealth through questionable means. “I implore the youths of today to be patient in everything they do,” he advised.
